TensorFlow files without TensorFlow

Source: vignettes/articles/tensorflow.Rmd
tensorflow.Rmd

Most of what TensorFlow writes to disk is Protocol Buffers:

  • a SavedModel (saved_model.pb) is a SavedModel message, holding the model’s graph (GraphDef) and its signatures;
  • a TFRecord file is a sequence of records, usually each a tf.train.Example, the format of many training data sets;
  • a TensorBoard log (events.out.tfevents.*) is a TFRecord file of Event messages: every loss and metric logged during training.

zuproto reads all three with TensorFlow’s schemas and nothing else: no Python and no TensorFlow installation. This article opens one of each.

The output below comes from a run on 27 October 2026. The code is not run when the site is built.

library(zuproto)

The schemas

TensorFlow’s .proto files are spread over its repository and import each other. This helper downloads the files a few top-level schemas need, following their imports, at one TensorFlow release. The schemas of the well-known types (google/protobuf/...) are built into every pool.

fetch_protos <- function(files, dir, ref = "v2.16.2") {
  base <- paste0(
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/",
    ref,
    "/"
  )
  # TSL's and XLA's schemas live under third_party/ in the repository.
  repo_path <- function(f) {
    if (startsWith(f, "tsl/")) {
      paste0("third_party/xla/third_party/tsl/", f)
    } else if (startsWith(f, "xla/")) {
      paste0("third_party/xla/", f)
    } else {
      f
    }
  }
  todo <- files
  done <- character()
  while (length(todo) > 0) {
    f <- todo[[1]]
    todo <- todo[-1]
    if (f %in% done || startsWith(f, "google/protobuf/")) {
      next
    }
    dest <- file.path(dir, f)
    dir.create(dirname(dest), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    download.file(paste0(base, repo_path(f)), dest, quiet = TRUE)
    imports <- grep("^import ", readLines(dest), value = TRUE)
    todo <- c(todo, sub('^import (public )?"(.*)";.*$', "\\2", imports))
    done <- c(done, f)
  }
  done
}

dir <- tempfile("tensorflow-")
protos <- fetch_protos(
  c(
    "tensorflow/core/protobuf/saved_model.proto",
    "tensorflow/core/example/example.proto",
    "tensorflow/core/util/event.proto"
  ),
  file.path(dir, "protos")
)
length(protos)
#> [1] 24

protoc, the protobuf compiler, turns the 24 files into one descriptor set. zuproto itself does not need protoc: on macOS, brew install protobuf; on Debian and Ubuntu, apt install protobuf-compiler.

desc <- file.path(dir, "tensorflow.binpb")
system2("protoc", c(
  paste0("--proto_path=", file.path(dir, "protos")),
  "--include_imports",
  paste0("--descriptor_set_out=", desc),
  protos
))
pool <- proto_pool(desc)
pool
#> <proto_pool: 35 files, 161 message types>

A SavedModel

TensorFlow’s own tests use a tiny SavedModel, half_plus_two, that computes y = 0.5 * x + 2. Its saved_model.pb is 10 kB.

saved <- file.path(dir, "saved_model.pb")
download.file(
  paste0(
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/v2.16.2/",
    "tensorflow/cc/saved_model/testdata/half_plus_two/00000123/",
    "saved_model.pb"
  ),
  saved,
  mode = "wb",
  quiet = TRUE
)
sm <- proto_decode(saved, "tensorflow.SavedModel", pool, defaults = FALSE)
mg <- sm$meta_graphs[[1]]
str(mg$meta_info_def[c("tags", "tensorflow_version")])
#> List of 2
#>  $ tags              : chr "serve"
#>  $ tensorflow_version: chr "1.1.0-rc2"

The signatures are the model’s entry points, the ones TensorFlow Serving exposes. A map field decodes to a named list.

signatures <- mg$signature_def
data.frame(
  name = names(signatures),
  method = vapply(signatures, \(s) s$method_name, ""),
  inputs = vapply(signatures, \(s) paste(names(s$inputs), collapse = ", "), ""),
  row.names = NULL
)
#>                name                      method inputs
#> 1 classify_x2_to_y3 tensorflow/serving/classify inputs
#> 2   classify_x_to_y tensorflow/serving/classify inputs
#> 3  regress_x2_to_y3  tensorflow/serving/regress inputs
#> 4    regress_x_to_y  tensorflow/serving/regress inputs
#> 5   regress_x_to_y2  tensorflow/serving/regress inputs
#> 6   serving_default  tensorflow/serving/predict      x

The graph is a GraphDef, the same message a frozen .pb graph file holds. Its 65 nodes are mostly the machinery for saving and restoring variables; counting the operators shows it.

nodes <- mg$graph_def$node
sort(table(vapply(nodes, \(n) n$op, "")), decreasing = TRUE)
#> 
#>              Const             Assign           Identity               NoOp 
#>                 24                  8                  8                  4 
#>         VariableV2                Add                Mul          RestoreV2 
#>                  4                  3                  3                  3 
#> MergeV2Checkpoints               Pack       ParseExample        Placeholder 
#>                  1                  1                  1                  1 
#>            Reshape             SaveV2    ShardedFilename         StringJoin 
#>                  1                  1                  1                  1

The model’s numbers are the initial values of its variables, constant tensors in the graph: a and b give 0.5 * x + 2, and the signatures ending in y3 add c instead of b. The dtype enum decodes to a factor.

consts <- Filter(\(n) grepl("initial_value$", n$name), nodes)
data.frame(
  node = vapply(consts, \(n) n$name, ""),
  dtype = vapply(consts, \(n) as.character(n$attr$dtype$type), "")
)
#>                            node     dtype
#> 1               a/initial_value  DT_FLOAT
#> 2               b/initial_value  DT_FLOAT
#> 3               c/initial_value  DT_FLOAT
#> 4 filename_tensor/initial_value DT_STRING
floats <- Filter(\(n) n$attr$dtype$type == "DT_FLOAT", consts)
vapply(floats, \(n) n$attr$value$tensor$float_val, 0)
#> [1] 0.5 2.0 3.0

Writing the other files

A TFRecord data set and a TensorBoard log come from running TensorFlow, so these were written by this Python script, from R’s faithful data set (write.csv(faithful, "faithful.csv", row.names = FALSE)). It stores each eruption as a tf.train.Example, then fits a small Keras model to predict an eruption’s length from the waiting time before it, logging to TensorBoard.

import os, sys
import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf

out = sys.argv[1]
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
data = np.genfromtxt(sys.argv[2], delimiter=",", skip_header=1)
eruption, waiting = data[:, 0], data[:, 1]
kind = np.where(eruption > 3, "long", "short")

with tf.io.TFRecordWriter(os.path.join(out, "eruptions.tfrecord")) as w:
    for i in range(len(waiting)):
        feature = {
            "waiting": tf.train.Feature(
                int64_list=tf.train.Int64List(value=[int(waiting[i])])),
            "eruption": tf.train.Feature(
                float_list=tf.train.FloatList(value=[eruption[i]])),
            "kind": tf.train.Feature(
                bytes_list=tf.train.BytesList(value=[kind[i].encode()])),
        }
        ex = tf.train.Example(features=tf.train.Features(feature=feature))
        w.write(ex.SerializeToString())

tf.keras.utils.set_random_seed(1)
x = (waiting - waiting.mean()) / waiting.std()
model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.Input((1,)),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(8, activation="relu"),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(1),
])
model.compile(optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(0.01), loss="mse",
              metrics=["mae"])
model.fit(x, eruption, epochs=40, validation_split=0.2, verbose=0,
          callbacks=[tf.keras.callbacks.TensorBoard(os.path.join(out, "logs"))])
files <- "tf-files" # the script's output directory

TFRecord files

A TFRecord file is not delimited the way proto_read_delimited() expects. Each record is its length as an 8-byte little-endian integer, a checksum of that length, the bytes, and a checksum of the bytes. Reading one takes a few lines of base R; this helper skips the CRC32C checksums rather than verifying them.

read_tfrecord <- function(path) {
  con <- file(path, "rb")
  on.exit(close(con))
  records <- list()
  repeat {
    len <- readBin(con, "raw", 8)
    if (length(len) == 0) {
      break
    }
    n <- sum(as.numeric(len) * 256^(0:7))
    readBin(con, "raw", 4) # CRC of the length
    records[[length(records) + 1]] <- readBin(con, "raw", n)
    readBin(con, "raw", 4) # CRC of the data
  }
  records
}

records <- read_tfrecord(file.path(files, "eruptions.tfrecord"))
length(records)
#> [1] 272

Each record is a tensorflow.Example. proto_decode_df() decodes them all at once; an Example keeps its values in a map of Features, each a list of bytes, floats or integers, so one more step makes columns of them.

ex <- proto_decode_df(records, "tensorflow.Example", pool)
features <- ex$features$feature
str(features[[1]])
#> List of 3
#>  $ eruption:List of 1
#>   ..$ float_list:List of 1
#>   .. ..$ value: num 3.6
#>  $ kind    :List of 1
#>   ..$ bytes_list:List of 1
#>   .. ..$ value:List of 1
#>   .. .. ..$ : raw [1:4] 6c 6f 6e 67
#>  $ waiting :List of 1
#>   ..$ int64_list:List of 1
#>   .. ..$ value: num 79

feature <- function(name) {
  vapply(features, \(f) {
    v <- f[[name]][[1]]$value
    if (is.list(v)) rawToChar(v[[1]]) else as.character(v)
  }, "")
}
eruptions <- data.frame(
  eruption = as.numeric(feature("eruption")),
  waiting = as.integer(feature("waiting")),
  kind = feature("kind")
)
head(eruptions)
#>   eruption waiting  kind
#> 1    3.600      79  long
#> 2    1.800      54 short
#> 3    3.333      74  long
#> 4    2.283      62 short
#> 5    4.533      85  long
#> 6    2.883      55 short

eruption was written as a 32-bit float, so it comes back as the nearest float to each value in faithful, not the value itself.

all.equal(eruptions$eruption, faithful$eruptions, tolerance = 1e-6)
#> [1] TRUE

TensorBoard logs

Keras writes one log for training and one for validation. Each is a TFRecord file of tensorflow.Events: a header, the model’s configuration, then one event per metric per epoch.

logs <- list.files(
  file.path(files, "logs"),
  pattern = "tfevents",
  recursive = TRUE,
  full.names = TRUE
)
basename(dirname(logs))
#> [1] "train"      "validation"
events <- read_tfrecord(logs[[1]])
str(proto_decode(events[[3]], "tensorflow.Event", pool, defaults = FALSE))
#> List of 2
#>  $ wall_time: num 1.79e+09
#>  $ summary  :List of 1
#>   ..$ value:List of 1
#>   .. ..$ :List of 3
#>   .. .. ..$ tag     : chr "epoch_loss"
#>   .. .. ..$ metadata:List of 1
#>   .. .. .. ..$ plugin_data:List of 1
#>   .. .. .. .. ..$ plugin_name: chr "scalars"
#>   .. .. ..$ tensor  :List of 3
#>   .. .. .. ..$ dtype         : Factor w/ 55 levels "DT_INVALID","DT_FLOAT",..: 2
#>   .. .. .. ..$ tensor_shape  : Named list()
#>   .. .. .. ..$ tensor_content: raw [1:4] d3 75 31 41

A scalar is a tensor of one 32-bit float, stored as four little-endian bytes in tensor_content. This turns a log into a table of step, metric and value.

read_scalars <- function(path) {
  rows <- lapply(read_tfrecord(path), \(r) {
    e <- proto_decode(r, "tensorflow.Event", pool)
    values <- Filter(
      \(v) identical(as.character(v$tensor$dtype), "DT_FLOAT"),
      e$summary$value
    )
    lapply(values, \(v) data.frame(
      step = e$step,
      tag = v$tag,
      value = readBin(v$tensor$tensor_content, "double", size = 4, endian = "little")
    ))
  })
  do.call(rbind, unlist(rows, recursive = FALSE))
}

scalars <- do.call(rbind, lapply(logs, \(path) {
  cbind(run = basename(dirname(path)), read_scalars(path))
}))
table(scalars$run, scalars$tag)
#>             
#>              epoch_learning_rate epoch_loss epoch_mae
#>   train                       40         40        40
#>   validation                   0         40        40
#>             
#>              evaluation_loss_vs_iterations evaluation_mae_vs_iterations
#>   train                                  0                            0
#>   validation                            40                           40

That is TensorBoard’s loss curve, as a data frame.

loss <- scalars[scalars$tag == "epoch_loss", ]
train <- loss[loss$run == "train", ]
valid <- loss[loss$run == "validation", ]
plot(
  train$step,
  train$value,
  type = "l",
  ylim = range(loss$value),
  xlab = "Epoch",
  ylab = "Mean squared error"
)
lines(valid$step, valid$value, lty = 2)
legend("topright", c("training", "validation"), lty = 1:2, bty = "n")

plot of chunk loss
